questionText: Which of the following organelles is responsible for the synthesis of proteins in the cell?
explanation: Ribosomes are the organelles responsible for protein synthesis. They translate messenger RNA (mRNA) into polypeptide chains. Ribosomes can be found free in the cytoplasm or attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum.

questionText: The organelle that is regarded as the powerhouse of the cell is the
explanation: The mitochondrion is called the powerhouse of the cell because it is the site where aerobic respiration occurs, producing ATP (adenosine triphosphate) which is the energy currency of the cell.

questionText: A distinguishing feature between a plant cell and an animal cell is that a plant cell has
explanation: Plant cells are distinguished from animal cells by the presence of a rigid cell wall made of cellulose and chloroplasts which contain chlorophyll for photosynthesis. While animal cells may have small vacuoles, the cell wall and chloroplasts are unique to plant cells.

questionText: During which stage of mitosis do chromosomes line up along the equator of the cell?
explanation: During metaphase, chromosomes align along the metaphase plate (equator) of the cell. The spindle fibres attach to the centromeres of each chromosome, positioning them at the centre of the cell before they are pulled apart in anaphase.

questionText: Meiosis is important in sexual reproduction because it

options.C: reduces the chromosome number by half

explanation: Meiosis is a reduction division that halves the chromosome number from diploid (2n) to haploid (n). This is important so that when two gametes fuse during fertilization, the diploid number is restored in the zygote, maintaining the chromosome number of the species across generations.

questionText: The process by which green plants manufacture their food using sunlight, water and carbon dioxide is called
explanation: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use sunlight energy, water and carbon dioxide to produce glucose and oxygen. The reaction occurs mainly in the leaves, specifically in the chloroplasts containing chlorophyll which absorbs light energy.

questionText: Which of the following minerals is required by plants for the formation of chlorophyll?
explanation: Magnesium is an essential component of chlorophyll, the green pigment in plants that absorbs light energy for photosynthesis. Without adequate magnesium, plants develop chlorosis (yellowing of leaves) because they cannot produce sufficient chlorophyll.

questionText: An insectivorous plant like the sundew traps insects to supplement its supply of
explanation: Insectivorous plants like the sundew grow in nitrogen-deficient soils (e.g., boggy or marshy habitats). They trap and digest insects to obtain nitrogen, which is essential for protein synthesis. The insect bodies provide amino acids and nitrogenous compounds the plant cannot get sufficiently from the soil.

questionText: The enzyme responsible for the digestion of starch in the mouth is
explanation: Ptyalin (salivary amylase) is the enzyme found in saliva that begins the digestion of starch in the mouth. It breaks down starch into maltose in the slightly alkaline conditions of the buccal cavity. Pepsin works on proteins in the stomach, trypsin on proteins in the duodenum, and lipase on fats.

questionText: The part of the alimentary canal where most absorption of digested food occurs is the
explanation: The ileum (the last and longest part of the small intestine) is the main site for the absorption of digested food. It is adapted for this function by having a large surface area due to villi and microvilli, a thin epithelial wall, a rich blood supply, and lacteals for fat absorption.

questionText: The vitamin whose deficiency causes night blindness is vitamin
explanation: Vitamin A (retinol) is essential for the formation of rhodopsin (visual purple), the light-sensitive pigment in the rod cells of the retina. Deficiency of vitamin A leads to night blindness (nyctalopia) where the individual cannot see well in dim light.

questionText: The tissue responsible for the transport of water and mineral salts from the roots to the leaves in plants is the
explanation: The xylem tissue is responsible for transporting water and dissolved mineral salts from the roots upwards to the leaves and other parts of the plant. Xylem vessels are dead, hollow tubes with lignified walls that provide both transport and structural support.

questionText: Transpiration pull in tall trees is maintained mainly by

options.B: cohesion and adhesion of water molecules

explanation: The transpiration pull (or cohesion-tension theory) explains the movement of water up tall trees. As water evaporates from the leaves, a tension is created that pulls water up through the xylem. This is possible because water molecules stick to each other (cohesion) and to the xylem walls (adhesion), forming an unbroken column of water.

questionText: Which of the following blood vessels carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs?
explanation: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle of the heart to the lungs for oxygenation. This is the only artery in the body that carries deoxygenated blood. The pulmonary vein, conversely, carries oxygenated blood from the lungs back to the left atrium of the heart.

questionText: The component of blood that is responsible for clotting is
explanation: Platelets (thrombocytes) are the blood components primarily responsible for blood clotting. When a blood vessel is damaged, platelets aggregate at the site and release thromboplastin, which triggers a cascade of reactions leading to the conversion of fibrinogen to fibrin, forming a clot.

questionText: A person with blood group AB can receive blood from
explanation: A person with blood group AB is called a universal recipient because their red blood cells carry both A and B antigens, and their plasma contains no anti-A or anti-B antibodies. Therefore, they can receive blood from donors of all ABO blood groups (A, B, AB, and O) without an agglutination reaction.

questionText: The end products of anaerobic respiration in yeast are
explanation: In yeast, anaerobic respiration (fermentation) breaks down glucose in the absence of oxygen to produce ethanol (alcohol) and carbon dioxide. This process is exploited in baking (CO2 makes bread rise) and brewing (ethanol is the desired product). In animals, anaerobic respiration produces lactic acid instead.

questionText: The site of the Krebs cycle in cellular respiration is the
explanation: The Krebs cycle (citric acid cycle) takes place in the matrix of the mitochondria. It is the second stage of aerobic respiration where acetyl CoA is oxidized to produce CO2, NADH, FADH2 and a small amount of ATP. Glycolysis, the first stage, occurs in the cytoplasm.

questionText: The functional unit of the kidney is the
explanation: The nephron is the functional unit of the kidney. Each kidney contains about one million nephrons. Each nephron consists of the Bowman's capsule (containing the glomerulus), proximal convoluted tubule, loop of Henle, distal convoluted tubule, and collecting duct. Together, these structures filter blood and produce urine.

questionText: Which of the following is NOT an excretory product in humans?
explanation: Faeces is not an excretory product but an egested material. Excretion refers to the removal of metabolic waste products from the body. Faeces consists mainly of undigested food that was never absorbed into the body cells and therefore was never part of metabolism. Urea, carbon dioxide, and bile pigments are true excretory products formed from metabolic processes.

questionText: The process by which the kidney filters blood under pressure in the Bowman's capsule is called
explanation: Ultrafiltration is the process by which blood is filtered under high pressure in the glomerulus of the Bowman's capsule. The high blood pressure in the glomerular capillaries forces small molecules (water, glucose, urea, salts, amino acids) through the capillary walls into the Bowman's capsule, while large molecules like proteins and blood cells are retained.

questionText: Pollination that involves the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of a different plant of the same species is called
explanation: Cross-pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther of one flower to the stigma of another flower on a different plant of the same species. This promotes genetic variation in the offspring. Self-pollination, in contrast, involves transfer within the same flower or between flowers on the same plant.

questionText: After fertilization in a flowering plant, the ovule develops into the
explanation: After fertilization in a flowering plant, the ovule develops into the seed. The ovule contains the embryo sac where fertilization occurs. The integuments of the ovule become the seed coat (testa), and the ovary wall develops into the fruit. The embryo and endosperm develop inside the seed.

questionText: The organ in the female reproductive system where the foetus develops is the
explanation: The uterus (womb) is the organ where the fertilized egg implants and the foetus develops throughout pregnancy. The uterus has a thick muscular wall and a rich blood supply through the placenta to nourish the developing foetus. The ovary produces eggs, and the fallopian tube is where fertilization usually occurs.

questionText: Which of the following hormones is responsible for the development of secondary sexual characteristics in males?
explanation: Testosterone is the male sex hormone produced by the testes (specifically the interstitial cells of Leydig). It is responsible for the development of secondary sexual characteristics in males such as deepening of the voice, growth of facial hair, broadening of shoulders, and increased muscle mass.

questionText: The type of germination in which the cotyledons are brought above the soil surface is called
explanation: Epigeal germination is the type of germination where the hypocotyl elongates, pushing the cotyledons above the soil surface. Examples include beans and groundnuts. In hypogeal germination, the epicotyl elongates and the cotyledons remain below the ground, as seen in maize and mango.

questionText: Metamorphosis is a process that occurs during the life cycle of
explanation: Metamorphosis is a biological process of transformation that occurs in many insects (and also amphibians). In complete metamorphosis, an insect passes through four stages: egg, larva, pupa, and adult (e.g., butterflies, houseflies). In incomplete metamorphosis, the insect passes through egg, nymph, and adult stages (e.g., cockroaches, grasshoppers).

questionText: The relationship between a tick feeding on a dog is an example of
explanation: The tick-dog relationship is parasitism because the tick (parasite) benefits by feeding on the blood of the dog (host), while the dog is harmed. In parasitism, one organism lives on or in another organism, deriving nutrients at the expense of the host. Unlike predation, the parasite does not usually kill the host immediately.

questionText: In a food chain, the organisms that occupy the first trophic level are the
explanation: Producers (green plants and autotrophs) occupy the first trophic level in a food chain. They are able to convert light energy into chemical energy through photosynthesis, making food available for all other organisms in the ecosystem. Primary consumers (herbivores) occupy the second trophic level.

questionText: The gradual replacement of one community of organisms by another in an area over time is known as
explanation: Ecological succession is the gradual and orderly process of change in an ecosystem brought about by the progressive replacement of one community by another until a stable climax community is established. Primary succession occurs on bare surfaces (e.g., rocks), while secondary succession occurs in areas where a community has been disturbed.

questionText: An example of a biotic factor in an ecosystem is
explanation: Biotic factors are living components or factors resulting from the activities of living organisms in an ecosystem. Competition (between organisms for resources) is a biotic factor. Rainfall, temperature, and humidity are abiotic (non-living) factors that influence the ecosystem.

questionText: In a cross between two heterozygous tall plants (Tt x Tt), the ratio of tall to short offspring expected is
explanation: When two heterozygous tall plants (Tt) are crossed, the offspring genotypes are TT, Tt, Tt, and tt (in the ratio 1:2:1). Since tallness (T) is dominant over shortness (t), TT and Tt are both tall, while only tt is short. Therefore, the phenotypic ratio is 3 tall : 1 short (3:1). This is Mendel's monohybrid ratio.

questionText: A sex-linked trait such as haemophilia is more common in males because

options.B: the gene is carried on the Y chromosome
options.C: males have only one X chromosome which may carry the recessive allele

explanation: Haemophilia is caused by a recessive allele on the X chromosome. Males (XY) have only one X chromosome, so if that X carries the haemophilia allele, they will express the condition since there is no corresponding allele on the smaller Y chromosome to mask it. Females (XX) would need two copies of the recessive allele to express the disease.

questionText: A change in the base sequence of DNA that may lead to a change in the characteristics of an organism is called
explanation: A mutation is a sudden change in the base sequence of DNA (gene mutation) or in chromosome number or structure (chromosomal mutation). Mutations can alter the proteins produced, potentially changing an organism's characteristics. Mutations can be spontaneous or induced by mutagens such as radiation or certain chemicals.

questionText: The theory of natural selection was proposed by
explanation: Charles Darwin proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection in his book 'On the Origin of Species' (1859). The theory states that organisms with favourable variations are better adapted to their environment, survive longer, reproduce more, and pass on their advantageous traits to their offspring (survival of the fittest).

questionText: Evidence of evolution can be obtained from all of the following EXCEPT
explanation: Blood group inheritance is a concept in genetics dealing with how ABO blood groups are passed from parents to offspring. It is not a direct line of evidence for evolution. Fossil records, comparative anatomy (homologous and analogous structures), and comparative embryology all provide strong evidence supporting the theory of evolution.

questionText: The binomial system of naming organisms was developed by
explanation: Carolus Linnaeus (Carl von Linne), a Swedish botanist, developed the binomial system of nomenclature in the 18th century. In this system, every organism is given two Latin names: the genus name (capitalized) and the species name (lowercase), both written in italics. For example, Homo sapiens for humans.

questionText: Which of the following groups of organisms belongs to the phylum Arthropoda?
explanation: Insects and crustaceans belong to the phylum Arthropoda, which is characterised by jointed appendages, segmented bodies, and an exoskeleton made of chitin. Other arthropod classes include arachnids (spiders) and myriapods (centipedes, millipedes). Snails belong to Mollusca, earthworms to Annelida, and starfish to Echinodermata.

questionText: Malaria in humans is caused by a protozoan belonging to the genus
explanation: Malaria is caused by protozoan parasites of the genus Plasmodium (e.g., Plasmodium falciparum, P. vivax, P. ovale, P. malariae). The parasite is transmitted to humans through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito. Trypanosoma causes sleeping sickness, and Entamoeba causes amoebic dysentery.

questionText: The process by which white blood cells engulf and destroy pathogens is called
explanation: Phagocytosis is the process by which white blood cells (phagocytes such as neutrophils and macrophages) engulf and digest invading pathogens. The phagocyte extends pseudopodia to surround the pathogen, forming a phagosome which then fuses with lysosomes containing digestive enzymes to destroy the pathogen. This is part of the body's innate immune response.

questionText: Which of the following diseases is caused by a virus?
explanation: Measles is caused by the measles virus (a paramyxovirus). It is a highly contagious disease spread through respiratory droplets. Cholera is caused by the bacterium Vibrio cholerae, tuberculosis by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and typhoid fever by Salmonella typhi. All three are bacterial diseases.

questionText: The part of the brain that controls and coordinates muscular activities and balance is the
explanation: The cerebellum is the part of the brain responsible for coordinating voluntary muscular movements, maintaining balance, posture, and muscle tone. It receives information from the sensory systems and the spinal cord and fine-tunes motor activity. The cerebrum handles thinking and consciousness, while the medulla oblongata controls involuntary actions like breathing and heartbeat.

questionText: A reflex action is one that is
explanation: A reflex action is an automatic, rapid, and involuntary response to a stimulus. It does not involve conscious thought and is coordinated by the spinal cord (spinal reflexes) or the lower brain centres (cranial reflexes). Examples include withdrawing the hand from a hot object, blinking, and the knee-jerk reflex.

questionText: The part of the eye that controls the amount of light entering it is the
explanation: The iris is the coloured part of the eye that controls the size of the pupil, thereby regulating the amount of light entering the eye. In bright light, the circular muscles of the iris contract to make the pupil smaller (constriction). In dim light, the radial muscles contract to make the pupil larger (dilation), allowing more light to enter.

questionText: The hormone insulin is produced by the
explanation: Insulin is produced by the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas. Insulin regulates blood sugar levels by promoting the uptake of glucose by body cells and the conversion of excess glucose to glycogen for storage in the liver and muscles. A deficiency of insulin leads to diabetes mellitus.

questionText: The hormone adrenaline prepares the body for
explanation: Adrenaline (epinephrine) is produced by the adrenal medulla and is known as the fight-or-flight hormone. When the body is under stress or in danger, adrenaline increases heart rate, raises blood pressure, dilates the pupils, increases blood sugar level, and diverts blood flow to the muscles, preparing the body to either confront or flee from the threat.

questionText: The type of joint found at the elbow is a
explanation: The elbow joint is a hinge joint, which allows movement in only one plane (flexion and extension), similar to a door hinge. The ball-and-socket joint (e.g., hip and shoulder) allows movement in multiple directions. A pivot joint (e.g., between atlas and axis vertebrae) allows rotational movement.

questionText: Muscles are attached to bones by
explanation: Tendons are tough, inelastic bands of fibrous connective tissue that attach muscles to bones. When a muscle contracts, the tendon pulls on the bone, causing movement. Ligaments, on the other hand, connect bone to bone and hold joints together. Cartilage reduces friction at joint surfaces.

questionText: The maintenance of a constant internal environment in living organisms is known as
explanation: Homeostasis is the maintenance of a stable and constant internal environment within an organism despite changes in the external environment. It involves the regulation of body temperature, blood sugar level, water and salt balance, pH, and other physiological parameters. Osmoregulation and thermoregulation are specific aspects of homeostasis.

questionText: When the blood sugar level rises above normal, the pancreas releases insulin which

options.C: breaks down proteins to amino acids

explanation: When blood sugar rises above normal (e.g., after a meal), the pancreas releases insulin which stimulates the liver and muscle cells to convert excess glucose to glycogen for storage. This brings the blood sugar level back to normal. When blood sugar drops below normal, the hormone glucagon is released, which converts stored glycogen back to glucose.
